name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q01 - Direct injection of sperm into ovum

questiontext.text: The method of directly injecting a sperm into ovum in Assisted Reproductive Technology is called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) include specialised procedures to help infertile couples conceive. When infertility is due to very low sperm count or inability of sperm to fertilise the ovum naturally, a specialised micromanipulation technique is used.

Step 2: Evaluation
In Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI), a single sperm is directly injected into the cytoplasm of the ovum in a laboratory to form an embryo. In contrast, GIFT involves transferring an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube, ZIFT involves transferring a zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube, and ET refers to embryo transfer into the uterus or fallopian tube.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the method of directly injecting a sperm into an ovum is ICSI.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q02 - Effect of IMR and MMR changes

questiontext.text: Increased IMR and decreased MMR in a population will:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) measures the death of infants per thousand live births, while Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) measures maternal deaths during pregnancy or childbirth. Population growth rate depends on the balance between births and deaths across all age groups.

Step 2: Evaluation
An increase in IMR means more infants die, which tends to decrease the population growth rate. Conversely, a decrease in MMR means more mothers survive childbirth, which tends to support population growth. Because these two changes act in opposing directions on the overall growth rate, their effects largely offset each other.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, increased IMR and decreased MMR in a population will not cause a significant change in growth rate.

answer.text: Not cause significant change in growth rate

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q03 - Reason intensely lactating mothers rarely conceive

questiontext.text: Intensely lactating mothers do not generally conceive due to the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Lactational amenorrhea is a natural method of contraception based on the absence of ovulation and menstruation during the period of intense lactation following parturition.

Step 2: Evaluation
High levels of the hormone prolactin, which is secreted during intense breastfeeding to stimulate milk production, inhibit the release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus. This suppresses the secretion of gonadotropins (LH and FSH) from the anterior pituitary, preventing ovarian follicular development and ovulation. It does not involve hypersecretion of gonadotropins, nor does it directly suppress gametic transport or fertilisation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, intensely lactating mothers do not generally conceive due to the suppression of gonadotropins.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q04 - Reasons sterilisation is a last option

questiontext.text:
Sterilisation techniques are generally fool proof methods of contraception with least side effects. Yet, this is the last option for the couples because:

i. It is almost irreversible
ii. Of the misconception that it will reduce sexual urge
iii. It is a surgical procedure
iv. Of lack of sufficient facilities in many parts of the country

Choose the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Surgical sterilisation methods (vasectomy in males and tubectomy in females) block gamete transport and thereby prevent conception permanently with minimal physiological side effects.

Step 2: Evaluation
Despite high efficacy, couples often treat sterilisation as a last resort for several practical and social reasons: the procedure is almost irreversible, limiting future family planning; there is a widespread misconception that sterilisation reduces sexual urge or drive; it requires a surgical procedure, which carries fear or hesitation; and adequate surgical and healthcare facilities are lacking in many parts of the country.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, all four factors—near-irreversibility, the misconception about reduced sexual urge, its surgical nature, and lack of sufficient facilities—explain why sterilisation is the last option for couples.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q05 - Initiation of national reproductive health approach

questiontext.text: A national level approach to build up a reproductively healthy society was taken up in our country in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
India was among the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal.

Step 2: Evaluation
These programmes, originally called "family planning", were initiated in India in 1951 and were periodically assessed over the subsequent decades, later expanding into broader Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the national-level approach to build a reproductively healthy society was taken up in the 1950s.

questiontext.text: Emergency contraceptives are effective if used within:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Emergency contraceptives (such as progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations, or IUDs) are used to prevent unwanted pregnancy after unprotected intercourse or contraceptive failure.

Step 2: Evaluation
To prevent ovulation, fertilisation, or implantation before pregnancy is established, emergency contraceptives must be administered within 72 hours of coitus. Waiting until 72 hours after implantation is ineffective because pregnancy has already occurred, and timing relative to ovulation or menstruation does not define the emergency contraceptive window.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, emergency contraceptives are effective if used within 72 hrs of coitus.

questiontext.text: Choose the right one among the statements given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) are effective and widely accepted contraceptives placed inside the uterus to prevent pregnancy.

Step 2: Evaluation
IUDs work primarily by increasing the phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus; copper-releasing IUDs also suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, while hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms. IUDs are inserted by doctors or expert nurses through the vagina into the uterus (not by the user herself), do not suppress gametogenesis, and have a finite lifespan requiring periodic replacement.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct statement is that IUDs increase phagocytosis reaction in the uterus.

answer.text: IUDs are generally inserted by the user herself
IUDs increase phagocytosis reaction in the uterus
IUDs once inserted need not be replaced

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q08 - Facts about Medical Termination of Pregnancy

questiontext.text:
Following statements are given regarding MTP. Choose the correct options given below:

i. MTPs are generally advised during first trimester
ii. MTPs are used as a contraceptive method
iii. MTPs are always surgical
iv. MTPs require the assistance of qualified medical personnel

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is the intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term, regulated to prevent misuse and ensure maternal safety.

Step 2: Evaluation
MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy) and must be performed with the assistance of qualified medical personnel to avoid fatal complications. However, MTPs are not meant to be used as a routine contraceptive method, and they are not always surgical because early pregnancies can also be terminated medically using prescribed drugs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct combination of statements is that MTPs are generally advised during the first trimester and require the assistance of qualified medical personnel.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q09 - STD not specifically affecting sex organs

questiontext.text: From the sexually transmitted diseases mentioned below, identify the one which does not specifically affect the sex organs:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs) are infections transmitted through sexual intercourse. While most STDs primarily infect the reproductive tract and sex organs, some affect systemic organs or the immune system.

Step 2: Evaluation
Syphilis, gonorrhoea, and genital warts are infections that directly affect the genital organs and reproductive tract. In contrast, Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), caused by HIV, specifically targets helper T-lymphocytes of the immune system rather than specifically affecting the sex organs.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, AIDS is the sexually transmitted disease that does not specifically affect the sex organs.

questiontext.text: Condoms are one of the most popular contraceptives because of the following reasons:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Condoms are barrier methods of contraception made of thin rubber or latex sheath used to cover the penis in the male or the vagina and cervix in the female just before coitus.

Step 2: Evaluation
Condoms act as effective physical barriers that prevent ejaculated semen from entering the female reproductive tract (preventing insemination). They are disposable, can be self-inserted, do not interfere with the coital act, and provide the additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs) such as AIDS.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, all of the stated reasons—acting as effective barriers for insemination, not interfering with the coital act, and reducing the risk of STDs—explain the popularity of condoms.

answer.text: They do not interfere with coital act
These help in reducing the risk of STDs

questiontext.text: Choose the correct statement regarding the ZIFT procedure:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer, an Assisted Reproductive Technology used following in vitro fertilisation (IVF).

Step 2: Evaluation
In ZIFT, the zygote or early embryo (with up to 8 blastomeres) formed in vitro is transferred into the fallopian tube of the female to continue development. Transferring an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube is GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer), whereas transferring an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus is IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct statement regarding ZIFT is that the zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the fallopian tube.

answer.text: Ova collected from a female donor are transferred to the fallopian tube to facilitate zygote formation.
Zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the fallopian tube
Zygote is collected from a female donor and transferred to the uterus
Ova collected from a female donor and transferred to the uterus

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q12 - Surgical procedure used as contraceptive method

questiontext.text: The correct surgical procedure as a contraceptive method is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Surgical sterilisation is a terminal contraceptive method that blocks gamete transport without removing the gonads or reproductive organs.

Step 2: Evaluation
Vasectomy is the surgical sterilisation procedure in males in which a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum. In contrast, ovariectomy (removal of ovaries), hysterectomy (removal of the uterus), and castration (removal of testes) are organ-removal surgeries performed for medical conditions rather than standard contraceptive procedures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, vasectomy is the correct surgical procedure used as a contraceptive method.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIVEHEALTH_MCQ_Q13 - Properties of diaphragms as female contraceptives

questiontext.text:
Diaphragms are contraceptive devices used by the females. Choose the correct option from the statements given below:

i. They are introduced into the uterus
ii. They are placed to cover the cervical region
iii. They act as physical barriers for sperm entry
iv. They act as spermicidal agents

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are reusable rubber barrier contraceptive devices designed for use by females.

Step 2: Evaluation
Diaphragms are inserted into the female reproductive tract (vagina) to cover the cervix during coitus, acting as physical barriers that block the entry of sperms through the cervix. They are not introduced into the uterus (unlike IUDs), and they are not spermicidal agents themselves, although spermicidal creams, jellies, or foams are often used along with them to increase contraceptive efficiency.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct characteristics of diaphragms are that they are placed to cover the cervical region and act as physical barriers for sperm entry.
